title: De las Heras: President Sheinbaum’s Approval Rises to 70% and Morena Also Grows, to 45%
author: Aranza Estrada
content:
_This article by[Aranza Estrada](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/aranza-
daniela-estrada-diaz/) originally appeared in the [November 2, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4897764/de-las-heras-la-aprobacion-de-
la-presidenta-sube-a-70-y-morena-crece-tambien-a-45/), an independent Mexican
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, November 2 (SinEmbargo).—** President [**Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/claudia-sheinbaum/) maintains broad
public support, with **70 percent approval** of her government and **67
percent positive opinions** of her performance, while **Morena** leads
electoral preferences for the **Chamber of Deputies** , according to the
National Household Public Opinion Survey by **De las Heras Demotecnia** for
October 2026.

The [results](https://www.demotecnia.com.mx/encuesta-nacional-octubre-2026/),
published this Monday, show that **51 percent of the people** surveyed have a
good opinion of the president and **16 percent** consider her very good,
compared to **19 percent** who express a negative assessment.

As for the [evaluation of her Administration](https://www.sinembargo.mx/pulso-
de-las-encuestas/aprobacion-de-la-presidenta-claudia-sheinbaum/), presidential
approval rose by approximately two percentage points compared to September,
when it stood at around 68 percent. In contrast, 24 percent of respondents
disapprove of her administration, while six percent did not respond.

![SinEmbargo chart showing the evolution of President Claudia Sheinbaum’s
approval rating between January 2025 and October
2026](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/02-approval-
trend.jpg)President Claudia Sheinbaum’s approval reached 70 percent in October
2026, while 24 percent disapprove of her administration. Photo: SinEmbargo

## Citizens Rate Sheinbaum’s Work at 7.2

In addition to approval levels, the De las Heras Demotecnia survey reveals
that the head of the federal Executive received an average rating of 7.2 out
of 10 for her work. Thirty-five percent of those interviewed gave her a score
of eight or nine, while 22 percent rated her administration with the highest
score.

In contrast, 18 percent gave her a rating of six or seven, 17 percent placed
her between one and five, and six percent gave her zero. Altogether, 57
percent of participants rated her performance at eight points or more.

Regarding the president’s honesty, 34 percent of those consulted consider her
very honest and 26 percent see her as somewhat honest, which represents a
favorable assessment of 60 percent on this indicator.

On the other hand, 19 percent believe she is not very honest and 13 percent
consider her not honest at all. Another two percent rated this attribute as
average, while six percent did not know or did not respond.

![Chart from the National Household Public Opinion Survey showing that 70
percent of respondents approve of Claudia Sheinbaum’s
administration](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/03-approval-chart-hd.jpg)Seven out of 10 Mexicans
approve of President Claudia Sheinbaum’s work, according to the October survey
by De las Heras Demotecnia. Photo: De las Heras Demotecnia

## Morena Leads the PAN by 36 Points in Electoral Preferences

Support for Morena is also reflected in electoral preferences, where the party
concentrates 45 percent of voting intention for the Chamber of Deputies, a
lead of 36 percentage points over the National Action Party (PAN), its closest
competitor, which registers nine percent.

According to the survey results, if the elections for federal deputies were
held today, preferences would be distributed as follows:

  * National Regeneration Movement (Morena): 45 percent.
  * National Action Party (PAN): nine percent.
  * Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI): seven percent.
  * Citizens’ Movement (MC): six percent.
  * Ecologist Green Party of Mexico (PVEM): four percent.
  * Labor Party (PT): two percent.
  * Partido Paz: one percent.
  * SomosMX: one percent.

In addition, 12 percent of those surveyed do not know whom they would vote
for, while 10 percent would not choose any political force. Another one
percent said they would not go to vote, one percent kept their preference
secret and one percent answered that they would vote for anyone.

Morena’s advantage is also seen in party identification, as 49 percent of
those interviewed say they feel closest to this political force, compared to
nine percent who identify with the PAN and eight percent with the PRI.
Citizens’ Movement has six percent, while the PVEM reaches three percent and
the PT two percent.

With these results, the party maintains a 40-percentage-point lead over
National Action in party identification, in addition to leading voting
intention by a wide margin heading into the next federal elections. In
contrast, 19 percent of respondents say they do not identify with any
political party.

![Chart from the De las Heras Demotecnia national survey for October 2026
showing voting intention for the Chamber of
Deputies](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/04-vote-
intention-hd.jpg)Morena leads electoral preferences with 45 percent of voting
intention for federal deputies, 36 points above the PAN. Photo: De las Heras
Demotecnia

## How Was the De las Heras Survey Conducted?

The De las Heras Demotecnia National Survey was conducted from October 23 to
26, 2026, through 1,000 interviews with people over 18 who hold a voter ID
card, with the aim of learning their perceptions of the federal government and
the population’s political preferences.

For the survey, the country’s electoral sections were divided into seven
strata, according to the type of electoral competition. The areas where the
questionnaires would be administered were then randomly selected, and
households were chosen through a systematic procedure with a random start.

The polling firm specified that the study has a 95 percent confidence level
and an expected statistical margin of error of ±3.2 percentage points, so its
results represent an estimate of public opinion during the survey period.
